Ole Dyg Pedersen is a Danish chief physician (*overlæge*) at Zealand University Hospital (*Sjællands Universitetshospital*) who plays a central role in the national quality assurance and clinical development of atrial fibrillation treatment in Denmark [^src1]. He is a key figure in the governance of the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database ([[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]]), serving as a member of its steering committee ([[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]]) [^src3]. 

His leadership within the organization has grown over time. While he is listed as a steering committee member in the 2023 annual report [^src1], by the 2024 and 2025 reporting periods, he is identified as the chairperson (*forperson*) for the database and the broader [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] initiative [^src2]. This initiative, documented in annual reports published by the Regional Clinical Quality Improvement Program (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute, tracks treatment quality, anticoagulation therapy, and patient outcomes across Danish health clusters [^src4]. Through his ongoing involvement from 2023 through 2025, Pedersen helps guide the shift from hospital-centered to population-based quality measurement, supporting both local clinical improvements and national healthcare policy [^src5].
